formal_rules: Every accepted expression has a specification-permitted type.
An operation requiring compatible types is valid only when the specified compatibility relation holds.
A read requires the place to contain a valid initialized value.
Destruction applies only to the initialized/partial ownership state permitted by the specification.
An owned value has exactly one responsible owner.
A move is valid only when the source currently owns an initialized value and no rule forbids invalidating it.
A copy is valid only when the type copy contract permits copying.
Shared borrowing is valid only when ownership, mutability, overlap, and lifetime constraints permit it.
A mutable borrow requires exclusive compatible access to the referent.
Overlapping capabilities must satisfy the applicable shared/mutable compatibility relation.
A capability may cease to constrain access only when no later semantic use requires it and doing so preserves behavior.
A borrow lifetime cannot exceed the referent lifetime.
A returned managed pointer derived from an input borrow cannot outlive that input borrow.
A control-flow join retains only semantic facts established on all applicable incoming paths, subject to specification rules.
Finite known cases must be exhaustively covered where the specification requires rejection of non-exhaustive matches.
Operands and function arguments are evaluated in the specified left-to-right order.
Successful initialization changes the semantic state from uninitialized to initialized.
A successful move transfers ownership responsibility and invalidates the source ownership state.
Copying creates an independent value and does not transfer ownership.
A shared capability is created without transferring ownership.
A mutable capability is created only when exclusive mutable access is permitted.
A derived capability does not transfer underlying ownership.
The previous owned destination value is replaced only after successful RHS evaluation.
A failed RHS evaluation does not replace the destination value.
Destruction consumes the applicable ownership/destruction responsibility exactly as specified.
Registration creates a future semantic use bound to the enclosing scope.
Deferred obligations execute before automatic destruction of the scope’s owned locals, in the specified order.
Return evaluates its expression before deferred blocks and destruction associated with exited scopes.
A failed operation produces no successful result and cannot be treated as having completed normally.
Cross-context ownership transfer creates exactly one destination ownership responsibility.
Successful join establishes the required happens-after relationship.
The specified synchronization relation establishes ordering and visibility.
An FFI call is valid only when ABI representation and explicit semantic contract obligations hold.
Unsafe context changes the permitted operation set but does not automatically create ownership, initialization, lifetime, or managed capability facts.
IR ⊢ V_type ∧ V_init ∧ V_owner ∧ V_borrow ∧ V_lifetime ∧ V_destroy ∧ V_control ∧ V_concurrent ∧ V_unsafe ∧ V_ffi
Validated semantic IR preserves the combined language safety model.
note: These normalized rules are derived from the existing semantic model; they do not add source syntax or implementation requirements.
